qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Rare disease portfolio (hematology/immunology) built largely via debt-fueled in-licensing and acquisitions rather than proprietary discovery, resulting in bloated intangibles and severe product write-downs.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). Sobi lacks an enduring organic R&D moat, relying on debt- and equity-fueled acquisitions to mask structural patent expirations in core hemophilia assets. Capital allocation missteps—epitomized by the SEK 17.1B acquisition of CTI BioPharma followed by a massive SEK 6.6B impairment on Vonjo in 2025—depress multi-cycle GAAP ROIC well below the 12% hurdle.
qualitative.evidence: Sobi's rare disease commercialization model has suffered heavy capital misallocation: the acquisition of CTI BioPharma underperformed commercially, forcing a SEK 6,612M pre-tax write-down in 2025 that crushed operating profit to SEK 867M and net income to SEK 478M. On an invested capital base bloated by goodwill and intangible rights (>SEK 35B), GAAP ROIC fell to low single digits in 2025, pulling 5-year median GAAP ROIC below the 12% requirement. Flagship hemophilia drugs (Elocta, Alprolix) face ongoing technological substitution.
